questions.question: Which group of words is an independent clause?
options: Because the rain stopped
When we arrived at the office
The clerk filed the documents
Although she was tired
After the meeting ended
questions.explanation: An independent clause has a subject and a verb and can stand alone. The other choices start with a subordinating word (because, when, although, after), so they are dependent clauses.

questions.question: In "The report that she submitted was complete," the group of words "that she submitted" is a:
options: independent clause
dependent (relative) clause
prepositional phrase
sentence fragment
compound predicate
questions.explanation: "That she submitted" has a subject and a verb but cannot stand alone. It describes "report", so it is a dependent (relative) clause.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly combines "The office closed early. The power was out."?
options: The office closed early because. The power was out.
The office closed early because the power was out.
Because the office closed early the power was out.
The office closed early, the power was out.
The office closed early although the power was out.
questions.explanation: "Because" shows that the power outage caused the early closing. The reversed order changes the meaning, the comma splice is incorrect, and "although" gives the wrong relationship.

questions.question: Which sentence contains a dependent clause that works as an adverb?
options: The manager who approved the leave resigned.
She smiled when the results came out.
The fact that he lied surprised us.
The employees are tired and hungry.
Submit the form today.
questions.explanation: "When the results came out" tells when she smiled, so it is an adverb clause. "Who approved the leave" describes a noun (adjective clause), and "that he lied" is a noun clause.

questions.question: What kind of sentence is "The employees complained, but the manager ignored them."?
options: Simple
Compound
Complex
Compound-complex
Fragment
questions.explanation: It has two independent clauses joined by "but" and no dependent clause, so it is compound.

questions.question: Which sentence is compound-complex?
options: We walked home because it rained.
We walked home, and we arrived late.
Although it rained, we walked home, and we arrived late.
We walked home.
Walking home in the rain.
questions.explanation: A compound-complex sentence has at least two independent clauses and one dependent clause. "Although it rained" is dependent; "we walked home" and "we arrived late" are independent.

questions.question: She likes swimming, reading, and ______.
options: to dance
dance
dancing
danced
dances
questions.explanation: Items in a series must have the same form. "Swimming" and "reading" are -ing forms, so the third item must be "dancing".

questions.question: Which sentence is parallel?
options: The job requires patience, being punctual, and to work hard.
The job requires patience, punctuality, and hard work.
The job requires being patient, punctuality, and to work hard.
The job requires patience, to be punctual, and working hard.
The job requires patient, punctuality, and work hard.
questions.explanation: "Patience, punctuality, and hard work" are all nouns, so the list is parallel.

questions.question: The manager told us to arrive early, to bring our IDs, and ______.
options: that we should sign in
signing in
to sign in at the gate
sign-in
we sign in
questions.explanation: The first two items are "to + verb" phrases, so the third must also be "to sign in".

questions.question: The candidate was both intelligent and ______.
options: with skill
skillfully
skilled
skill
had skills
questions.explanation: "Both ... and" joins equal parts. "Intelligent" is an adjective, so the second part must be an adjective: "skilled".

questions.question: Not only did she finish the report, but she also ______.
options: the presentation was prepared
prepared the presentation
preparing the presentation
to prepare the presentation
presentation preparation
questions.explanation: After "not only did she finish", the second part needs the same verb pattern: "she also prepared the presentation".

questions.question: Which sentence has faulty parallelism?
options: He is not only a skilled driver but also a careful one.
She enjoys hiking, to swim, and cycling.
The plan is simple, practical, and affordable.
To plan well and to execute carefully are keys to success.
We want to save money and to reduce waste.
questions.explanation: "Hiking, to swim, and cycling" mixes -ing forms with an infinitive. It should be "hiking, swimming, and cycling".

questions.question: Which sentence has a dangling modifier?
options: Walking to work, a dog barked at Jose.
Walking to work, Jose saw a dog.
Jose, walking to work, saw a dog.
While Jose walked to work, a dog barked at him.
Jose saw a dog while walking to work.
questions.explanation: In the first sentence, "walking to work" seems to describe the dog. The person walking is Jose, so the modifier dangles.

questions.question: Which sentence is clear and correct?
options: The clerk handed the folder to the supervisor that was blue.
The clerk handed the supervisor the blue folder.
The clerk handed to the supervisor the folder blue.
Blue, the clerk handed the folder to the supervisor.
The blue clerk handed the folder.
questions.explanation: The modifier "blue" must sit next to the folder it describes. In the first choice, "that was blue" seems to describe the supervisor.

questions.question: Which sentence means that she drove for nearly two hours?
options: She almost drove for two hours.
She drove for almost two hours.
Almost, she drove two hours.
She drove almost, for two hours.
For two hours almost she drove.
questions.explanation: "Almost" should sit right before "two hours". "She almost drove" means she nearly did it but did not.

questions.question: Which is the best revision of "Having finished the exam, the papers were handed in."?
options: Having finished the exam, the examinees handed in their papers.
Having finished the exam, the papers were handed in by the proctor.
Having finished, the exam papers were handed in.
The papers, having finished the exam, were handed in.
Having been finished the exam, the papers were handed in.
questions.explanation: Papers cannot finish an exam. The subject after the comma must be the one who finished: "the examinees".

questions.question: Which sentence clearly states that the employees, not the supervisor, arrived late?
options: The employees were reprimanded by the supervisor who arrived late.
The employees who arrived late were reprimanded by the supervisor.
Reprimanded by the supervisor, arriving late was the employees.
Late arriving, the supervisor reprimanded employees who.
The employees were arriving late who the supervisor reprimanded.
questions.explanation: The modifier "who arrived late" must come right after "employees". In the first choice it follows "supervisor".

questions.question: Which sentence means that Maria and no one else won the prize?
options: Maria only won the prize.
Only Maria won the prize.
Maria won only the prize.
Maria won the only prize.
Maria won the prize only.
questions.explanation: "Only" belongs right before the word it limits. "Only Maria" limits the winner to Maria.

questions.question: Which is a complete sentence?
options: Because the bus was late.
Running down the street.
The bus was late.
The bus, which was late.
When the bus came.
questions.explanation: Only "The bus was late." has a subject and a verb and expresses a complete thought. The others are fragments.

questions.question: Which sentence is a run-on?
options: The office opens at eight it closes at five.
The office opens at eight, and it closes at five.
The office opens at eight; it closes at five.
The office opens at eight and closes at five.
The office, which opens at eight, closes at five.
questions.explanation: Two independent clauses are joined with no punctuation or conjunction. A comma with "and", or a semicolon, would fix it.

questions.question: Which sentence is a comma splice?
options: I called twice, but nobody answered.
I called twice, nobody answered.
I called twice; nobody answered.
I called twice, yet nobody answered.
Although I called twice, nobody answered.
questions.explanation: A comma alone cannot join two independent clauses. A conjunction such as "but" or a semicolon is needed.

questions.question: Which sentence is the most concise?
options: Due to the fact that it was raining, the event was postponed.
Because it rained, the event was postponed.
The reason the event was postponed was because of the rain that was falling.
The event was postponed on account of the fact of rain.
It was raining and so the event was postponed due to this.
questions.explanation: "Because it rained" says the same thing in fewer words. The others repeat the cause.

questions.question: Which choice corrects the fragment "The applicants waiting outside the office since morning."?
options: The applicants waiting outside the office since morning were tired.
The applicants waiting outside the office since morning, tired.
Waiting outside the office since morning the applicants.
The applicants, waiting outside the office since morning.
The applicants which waiting outside the office since morning.
questions.explanation: The original has a subject but no main verb. Adding "were tired" gives the sentence a predicate.

questions.question: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
options: The budget was cut, however the project continued.
The budget was cut; however, the project continued.
The budget was cut; however the project, continued.
The budget was cut however; the project continued.
The budget was cut, however, the project continued.
questions.explanation: A conjunctive adverb such as "however" joining two independent clauses needs a semicolon before it and a comma after it.
